points: P1: "guarded"; begin with orientation and containment instead of adding depth (a directive)
was: Inductions serve to gather up attention in order to access quiet stuff. They are not about surrendering, playing asleep, or obeying someone. You may want to do an actual induction if you are sober, distracted, analytical, or otherwise not very trancey. You can skip the induction and go straight to orientation and containment if you are already trancey, due to meditation, loveyhuasca, lucid dreaming, grief, music, prayer, or tiredness, or if for any other reason you feel in touch with deeper stuff.
new: Inductions serve to gather up attention in order to access quiet stuff. They are not about surrendering, playing asleep, or obeying someone. You may want to do an actual induction if you are sober, distracted, analytical, guarded, or otherwise not very trancey. If you are already trancey, due to meditation, loveyhuasca, lucid dreaming, grief, music, prayer, or tiredness, or if for any other reason you feel in touch with deeper stuff, skip the induction and go straight to orientation and containment instead of going deeper.

points: P2: the amount of trance that suits the practice, and its qualities (focused, warm, receptive, embodied, still able to stop); out: "You can control and decide how trancey you want to get" (invented)
was: You can control and decide how trancey you want to get. Deeper trance is optional.
new: Get as trancey as the practice needs: focused, warm, receptive, embodied, and still able to stop. Deeper trance is optional.

points: P4: deepen only when that helps; let what you notice shape the words and the next response
was: It gets you ready to do whatever you are doing. It does this by gathering up your attention, deepening the state, and then utilizing that state to say more things that make that state more likely. There are all sorts of ways to do this. The method here involves counting, but there are many others. You might just talk with someone, tell a story, move, play with sound, or make use of curiosity. However you do it, say so. Don’t pretend it’s some other thing in the name of elegance.
new: It gets you ready to do whatever you are doing. It does this by gathering up your attention, deepening the state only when that helps, and then letting what you notice shape the words and what happens next. There are all sorts of ways to do this. The method here involves counting, but there are many others. You might just talk with someone, tell a story, move, play with sound, or make use of curiosity. However you do it, say so. Don’t pretend it’s some other thing in the name of elegance.

points: P5: build from the response that is already happening; a receptive way of listening (not "what you want to hear"); no ceremony to finish before you may respond; out: "always"
was: You can always test a simple target suggestion before deepening, to see if you are already getting your target response, and then deepen from that, if needed. The induction is just there to get you into a place from which to listen to what you want to hear. It doesn’t have to be some sort of ceremony.
new: You can test a simple target suggestion before deepening, to see if you are already getting your target response, and then build from that. The induction is just there to help you find a receptive way of listening. It doesn’t have to be some sort of ceremony you finish before you’re allowed to respond.

points: P7: neutral witnessing; the metaphors needn't all report for duty at once (not "you don't need" them); switch when the metaphor stops helping
was: You need to keep it simple. One purpose, one anchor or image to start, one way back, and a decided on feeling (warm, bounded, directed, or neutral). You don’t need floating, stairs, gardens, inner rooms, color, or a dialogue with a child. If you do metaphors at all, use one, and only switch to another consciously.
new: You need to keep it simple. One purpose, one anchor or image to start, one way back, and a decided on feeling (warm, bounded, directed, or neutral witnessing). You don’t need floating, stairs, gardens, inner rooms, color, and a dialogue with a child all at once. If you do metaphors at all, use one, and only switch to another consciously, when the first one stops helping.

points: P8: a signal arrives (the reader doesn't send one)
was: Metaphors and imagery are optional. You might signal and receive signal through sensation, rhythm, movement, words, spatial sense, simple knowing, or the lack of a signal. If you are using words, keep them related to the world you have created. If you are counting, do it in a way that makes sense in that world. When you’re done with your induction, come back the other way. You can borrow qualities from your induction (warmth or steadiness) but don’t change who you are.
new: Metaphors and imagery are optional. A signal might come to you through sensation, rhythm, movement, words, spatial sense, simple knowing, or the lack of a signal. If you are using words, keep them related to the world you have created. If you are counting, do it in a way that makes sense in that world. When you’re done with your induction, come back the other way. You can borrow qualities from your induction (warmth or steadiness) but don’t change who you are.

points: P11: you don't have to find a problem; several minutes for returning and reflecting

Make sure to leave time at the end for coming back and for reflection.

points: P12: get immediate support instead of exploratory hypnosis; Already open? is for orientation, not for intensifying an unstable state

points: P13: a firmer invitation to stay with a feeling; out: "a gentle suggestion" (added)
was: 4. Decide how you want to be coaxed into it. Do you want to feel like you have a lot of room, or do you want to feel held and warm? Do you need more firm direction, or are you fine with a gentle suggestion? Preview to yourself what you are going to do. This might involve closing your eyes, or even coming out of it and going back in. It will include coming back at the end. If you are recording your induction, read the script to yourself first (if you can). Know that you can end the induction any time you want by saying “stop” or by opening your eyes. You can also say “less” to make it ask less of you, or “quiet” to make it stop talking. You do not need permission from any inner part to stop, even if you feel like a part is telling you that you need permission.

points: P14: let a useful response become easier and less effortful (an invitation); silence doesn't authorize a narrator to add what you haven't agreed to (a consent rule)
was: 5. If you have not done hypnosis before, or if you haven’t done it in a while, practice the coming in and out part first before trying to do it for anything else. You don’t have to watch yourself the whole time, but it is good to make sure you can do the state change at first. You are making something easier, so it will require less work. The answer no will stay no. Silence won’t create a narrator who says things you didn’t.

And if you say nothing, that isn’t a yes, so a narrator can’t add things you haven’t agreed to.

points: P57: what fractionation is (back toward ordinary awareness, then deciding whether to go back in); used openly, a door in both directions; name it before using it (not "I always announce", an invented fact); no answer secretly means "deeper"
was: There is an optional fractionation you can add to this at some point. I always announce when I am doing it and note that I am breaking the pattern of always going deeper at each answer.
new: There is an optional fractionation you can add to this at some point: you come back toward ordinary awareness, then decide whether to go back in. Used openly, it teaches you that trance has a door in both directions. Say that you're doing it before you do it, so an answer never secretly means "go deeper".

points: P58: open your eyes and come back toward ordinary awareness (a step); feel the room; notice what changes as attention gathers again; you may stop at either point

new: Open your eyes and come back up toward ordinary awareness. Feel the room and decide whether to stop here. If you want to go on, close or soften your eyes again and notice what changes as your attention gathers. Either way is ok, you can stop at either point.

points: P60: if it is useful, attention may become more gathered

new: If it will be useful, your attention may gather more. But if it won't, you can stay just as awake as you need to be.

points: P75: state your decision while awake; a cancellation sentence doesn't prove the association vanished instantly; persistent unwanted responses or disorientation need qualified help; a retained cue is only for a future, separately chosen session; today's state ends with the return; out: "something like the below" (twice, with nothing below) and "a good start"
was: To turn it off, just stop rehearsing it, remove it from any recordings you may have, stop having it as an active part of any apps you may use, and go back to the regular induction. You can say something like the below when you are awake to indicate that you are done using it, but keep in mind that saying something doesn't make it true. If you feel you still have the response when you don't want it, or you feel disoriented after the state, please get qualified help. Just saying something like the below doesn't necessarily make it true, but it is a good start. If you want to keep it for future use, indicate that you will only use it to begin a session at a future time, and that the state you are in now is ending.
